0001: // Runtime for generated differential self-tests (tools/decomp/autotest.py).
0002: // Each case builds the same object state and arguments, then runs the original
0003: // function and the decompiled one in two forked children of the game process.
0004: // The children report the return value and the bytes of the object and its
0005: // fake collaborators; any difference fails the test. Identical crashes are
0006: // inconclusive. A resource timeout is an incomplete observation on either side.
0007: #ifndef AUTOTEST_H
0008: #define AUTOTEST_H
0009: 
0010: #include <cstring>
0011: #include <errno.h>
0012: #include <malloc.h>
0013: #include <new>
0014: #include <string>
0015: #include <signal.h>
0016: #include <stdint.h>
0017: #include <sys/prctl.h>
0018: #include <sys/time.h>
0019: #include <sys/wait.h>
0020: #include <time.h>
0021: #include <unistd.h>

0023: #include "HybridTest.h"

0028: struct Rng
0029: {
0030:     uint64_t state;
0031:     explicit Rng(uint64_t seed) : state(seed * 2654435761u + 1) {}
0032:     unsigned int next()
0033:     {
0034:         state = state * 6364136223846793005ULL + 1442695040888963407ULL;
0035:         return (unsigned int)(state >> 33);
0036:     }
0037: };
0038: 
0039: // Values close to the boundaries code usually tests, plus random ones.
0040: inline long long randomInt(Rng& r)
0041: {
0042:     static const long long picks[] = {0, 1, -1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10, 16, 100, -2, -100, 255, 1000};
0043:     unsigned int k = r.next() % 20;
0044:     if (k < sizeof(picks) / sizeof(picks[0]))
0045:         return picks[k];
0046:     return (long long)(r.next() % 2001) - 1000;
0047: }
0048: 
0049: inline double randomFloat(Rng& r)
0050: {
0051:     static const double picks[] = {0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 0.5, 2.0, -0.25, 10.0, 0.001, 100.0};
0052:     unsigned int k = r.next() % 14;
0053:     if (k < sizeof(picks) / sizeof(picks[0]))
0054:         return picks[k];
0055:     return ((double)(r.next() % 20001) - 10000.0) / 100.0;
0056: }
0057: 
0058: inline const wchar_t* randomText(Rng& r)
0059: {
0060:     static const wchar_t* picks[] = {L"", L"a", L"TEST", L"Hello World", L"media/test.dat", L"0", L"12"};
0061:     return picks[r.next() % (sizeof(picks) / sizeof(picks[0]))];
0062: }
0063: 
0064: // Arena for the object under test and fake collaborators: same addresses in
0065: // both children, so pointers into it compare equal.
0066: const size_t kArenaSize = 1 << 20;
0067: extern char g_arena[kArenaSize];
0068: extern size_t g_arenaUsed;
0069: 
0070: inline void* allocate(size_t size)
0071: {
0072:     size_t at = (g_arenaUsed + 15) & ~(size_t)15;
0073:     if (at + size > kArenaSize)
0074:         return 0;
0075:     g_arenaUsed = at + size;
0076:     std::memset(g_arena + at, 0, size);
0077:     return g_arena + at;
0078: }
0079: 
0080: inline bool inArena(const void* p)
0081: {
0082:     uintptr_t at = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(p);
0083:     uintptr_t start = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(g_arena);
0084:     return at >= start && at - start < kArenaSize;
0085: }
0086: 
0087: // Fake objects made for a case, by class; arguments and list elements
0088: // sometimes reuse them, so lookups and removals find what they look for.
0089: struct Pool
0090: {
0091:     enum { kSize = 256 };
0092:     void* pointer[kSize];
0093:     int kind[kSize];
0094:     int count;
0095: };
0096: extern Pool g_pool;
0097: 
0098: inline void remember(void* p, int kind)
0099: {
0100:     if (g_pool.count < Pool::kSize)
0101:     {
0102:         g_pool.pointer[g_pool.count] = p;
0103:         g_pool.kind[g_pool.count] = kind;
0104:         g_pool.count++;
0105:     }
0106: }
0107: 
0108: inline void* pick(Rng& r, int kind, void* fresh)
0109: {
0110:     int n = 0;
0111:     for (int i = 0; i < g_pool.count; i++)
0112:         n += g_pool.kind[i] == kind && g_pool.pointer[i] != fresh;
0113:     if (n == 0 || r.next() % 3 == 0)
0114:         return fresh;
0115:     int k = r.next() % n;
0116:     for (int i = 0; i < g_pool.count; i++)
0117:         if (g_pool.kind[i] == kind && g_pool.pointer[i] != fresh && k-- == 0)
0118:             return g_pool.pointer[i];
0119:     return fresh;
0120: }
0121: 
0122: struct Capture
0123: {
0124:     enum { kSize = 256 * 1024 };
0125:     enum Issue { Complete = 0, Overflow = 1, UnsupportedPointer = 2, InvalidReport = 3 };
0126:     size_t length;
0127:     unsigned int issue;
0128:     char data[kSize];
0129: 
0130:     void reset()
0131:     {
0132:         length = 0;
0133:         issue = Complete;
0134:     }
0135:     void add(const void* p, size_t n)
0136:     {
0137:         if (issue != Complete)
0138:             return;
0139:         // A bounded buffer is intentional; an unobserved tail is never equal.
0140:         if (length > kSize || n > kSize - length)
0141:         {
0142:             issue = Overflow;
0143:             return;
0144:         }
0145:         if (!n)
0146:             return;
0147:         std::memcpy(data + length, p, n);
0148:         length += n;
0149:     }
0150:     void addPointer(const void* p)
0151:     {
0152:         if (issue != Complete)
0153:             return;
0154:         // Pool's generated fake objects live in the arena and retain identity
0155:         // across forks. Child allocations and other external pointers have no
0156:         // logical identity here; neither raw addresses nor malloc totals prove it.
0157:         if (p && !inArena(p))
0158:         {
0159:             issue = UnsupportedPointer;
0160:             return;
0161:         }
0162:         long long token = p == 0 ? 0 : 1 + ((const char*)p - g_arena);
0163:         add(&token, sizeof(token));
0164:     }
0165:     // Bytes in use on the malloc heap: both children start from the same heap,
0166:     // so a missing delete or an extra allocation shows here.
0167:     void addHeapInUse()
0168:     {
0169:         struct mallinfo info = mallinfo();
0170:         long long used = info.uordblks;
0171:         add(&used, sizeof(used));
0172:     }
0173:     void addText(const std::wstring& s)
0174:     {
0175:         if (issue != Complete)
0176:             return;
0177:         size_t n = s.size();
0178:         add(&n, sizeof(n));
0179:         if (n > kSize / sizeof(wchar_t))
0180:         {
0181:             issue = Overflow;
0182:             return;
0183:         }
0184:         add(s.data(), n * sizeof(wchar_t));
0185:     }
0186: };
0187: 
0188: // Return values of any type (void included) through the comma operator.
0189: struct Void
0190: {
0191: };
0192: template <class T>
0193: struct Value
0194: {
0195:     T value;
0196: };
0197: template <class T>
0198: Value<T> operator,(const T& value, Void)
0199: {
0200:     Value<T> v = {value};
0201:     return v;
0202: }
0203: inline void record(Capture&, Void) {}
0204: template <class T>
0205: void record(Capture& out, const Value<T>& v)
0206: {
0207:     out.add(&v.value, sizeof(T));
0208: }
0209: template <class T>
0210: void record(Capture& out, const Value<T*>& v)
0211: {
0212:     out.addPointer(v.value);
0213: }
0214: inline void record(Capture& out, const Value<std::wstring>& v)
0215: {
0216:     out.addText(v.value);
0217: }
0218: inline void record(Capture& out, const Value<bool>& v)
0219: {
0220:     unsigned char b = v.value ? 1 : 0;
0221:     out.add(&b, 1);
0222: }
0223: 
0224: typedef void (*Body)(void* context, Capture& out);
0225: 
0226: struct Outcome
0227: {
0228:     // status stays compatible with handwritten tests: clean exit is exposed
0229:     // only when a complete report arrived. childStatus is the actual wait status.
0230:     int status;
0231:     int childStatus;
0232:     bool reportValid;
0233:     bool reportStarted;
0234:     Capture capture;
0235: };
0236: 
0237: extern Outcome g_outcomes[2];
0238: 
0239: inline void crashed(int signal)
0240: {
0241:     _exit(128 + signal);
0242: }
0243: 
0244: struct ReportHeader
0245: {
0246:     uint32_t magic;
0247:     uint32_t version;
0248:     uint32_t length;
0249:     uint32_t issue;
0250: };
0251: const uint32_t kReportMagic = 0x544c4350;
0252: // Reserved by the observer; a failed pipe write is not a function failure.
0253: const int kReportWriteFailure = 253;
0254: 
0255: inline bool writeExact(int fd, const void* data, size_t length)
0256: {
0257:     const char* at = (const char*)data;
0258:     while (length)
0259:     {
0260:         ssize_t n = write(fd, at, length);
0261:         if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR)
0262:             continue;
0263:         if (n <= 0)
0264:             return false;
0265:         at += n;
0266:         length -= n;
0267:     }
0268:     return true;
0269: }
0270: 
0271: inline bool readExact(int fd, void* data, size_t length, size_t* completed = 0)
0272: {
0273:     char* at = (char*)data;
0274:     if (completed)
0275:         *completed = 0;
0276:     while (length)
0277:     {
0278:         ssize_t n = read(fd, at, length);
0279:         if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR)
0280:             continue;
0281:         if (n <= 0)
0282:             return false;
0283:         at += n;
0284:         length -= n;
0285:         if (completed)
0286:             *completed += n;
0287:     }
0288:     return true;
0289: }
0290: 
0291: inline bool writeReport(int fd, const Capture& capture)
0292: {
0293:     ReportHeader header = {kReportMagic, 1, (uint32_t)capture.length, capture.issue};
0294:     return writeExact(fd, &header, sizeof(header)) && writeExact(fd, capture.data, capture.length);
0295: }
0296: 
0297: inline bool readReport(int fd, Capture& capture, bool* started = 0)
0298: {
0299:     capture.reset();
0300:     capture.issue = Capture::InvalidReport;
0301:     ReportHeader header;
0302:     size_t headerBytes;
0303:     bool gotHeader = readExact(fd, &header, sizeof(header), &headerBytes);
0304:     if (started)
0305:         *started = headerBytes != 0;
0306:     if (!gotHeader || header.magic != kReportMagic || header.version != 1 ||
0307:         header.length > Capture::kSize || header.issue > Capture::UnsupportedPointer ||
0308:         !readExact(fd, capture.data, header.length))
0309:         return false;
0310:     // Exactly one frame, including EOF, is required; no trailing partial frame.
0311:     char extra;
0312:     ssize_t n;
0313:     do { n = read(fd, &extra, 1); } while (n < 0 && errno == EINTR);
0314:     if (n != 0)
0315:         return false;
0316:     capture.length = header.length;
0317:     capture.issue = header.issue;
0318:     return true;
0319: }
0320: 
0321: // Runs body in a forked child; the child reports its capture through a pipe.
0322: inline void runChild(Body body, void* context, Outcome& outcome, unsigned cpuMs = 300, unsigned wallMs = 3000)
0323: {
0324:     int fds[2];
0325:     outcome.capture.reset();
0326:     outcome.capture.issue = Capture::InvalidReport;
0327:     outcome.status = -1;
0328:     outcome.childStatus = -1;
0329:     outcome.reportValid = false;
0330:     outcome.reportStarted = false;
0331:     if (pipe(fds) != 0)
0332:         return;
0333:     pid_t pid = fork();
0334:     if (pid == 0)
0335:     {
0336:         close(fds[0]);
0337:         // A crash ends the child at once: no game crash handler, no core dump.
0338:         prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0, 0, 0, 0);
0339:         signal(SIGSEGV, crashed);
0340:         signal(SIGBUS, crashed);
0341:         signal(SIGFPE, crashed);
0342:         signal(SIGILL, crashed);
0343:         signal(SIGABRT, crashed);
0344:         signal(SIGALRM, SIG_DFL);
0345:         signal(SIGPROF, SIG_DFL);
0346:         struct itimerval limit;
0347:         std::memset(&limit, 0, sizeof(limit));
0348:         // CPU includes system time; scheduler delays must not consume this budget.
0349:         limit.it_value.tv_sec = cpuMs / 1000;
0350:         limit.it_value.tv_usec = (cpuMs % 1000) * 1000;
0351:         if (!cpuMs) limit.it_value.tv_usec = 1000;
0352:         setitimer(ITIMER_PROF, &limit, 0);
0353:         // A separate wall deadline still catches blocked IO/locks.
0354:         limit.it_value.tv_sec = wallMs / 1000;
0355:         limit.it_value.tv_usec = (wallMs % 1000) * 1000;
0356:         if (!wallMs) limit.it_value.tv_usec = 1000;
0357:         setitimer(ITIMER_REAL, &limit, 0);
0358:         // A child-local buffer also lets hand-written tests call runChild
0359:         // without linking the generated runtime's global outcome storage.
0360:         Capture capture;
0361:         capture.reset();
0362:         body(context, capture);
0363:         if (!writeReport(fds[1], capture))
0364:             _exit(kReportWriteFailure);
0365:         _exit(0);
0366:     }
0367:     close(fds[1]);
0368:     if (pid > 0)
0369:         outcome.reportValid = readReport(fds[0], outcome.capture, &outcome.reportStarted);
0370:     close(fds[0]);
0371:     if (pid > 0)
0372:     {
0373:         int status;
0374:         pid_t waited;
0375:         do { waited = waitpid(pid, &status, 0); } while (waited < 0 && errno == EINTR);
0376:         if (waited == pid)
0377:         {
0378:             outcome.childStatus = status;
0379:             outcome.status = status;
0380:             if (WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0 &&
0381:                 (!outcome.reportValid || outcome.capture.issue != Capture::Complete))
0382:                 outcome.status = 4 << 8;
0383:         }
0384:     }
0385: }
0386: 
0387: struct Stats
0388: {
0389:     int same;
0390:     int bothFailed;
0391:     int different;
0392:     int incomplete;
0393: };
0394: 
0395: inline bool incomplete(const Outcome& outcome)
0396: {
0397:     if (outcome.childStatus < 0 || (outcome.reportStarted && !outcome.reportValid) ||
0398:         (outcome.reportValid && outcome.capture.issue != Capture::Complete))
0399:         return true;
0400:     if (WIFSIGNALED(outcome.childStatus) &&
0401:         (WTERMSIG(outcome.childStatus) == SIGALRM || WTERMSIG(outcome.childStatus) == SIGPROF))
0402:         return true;
0403:     return WIFEXITED(outcome.childStatus) &&
0404:            (WEXITSTATUS(outcome.childStatus) == kReportWriteFailure ||
0405:             (WEXITSTATUS(outcome.childStatus) == 0 && !outcome.reportValid));
0406: }
0407: 
0408: // One differential case; incomplete observation is separate from a difference.
0409: inline bool compareCase(Body original, Body ours, void* context, Stats& stats, const tlhybrid_host* host,
0410:                         const char* name, int index)
0411: {
0412:     runChild(original, context, g_outcomes[0]);
0413:     runChild(ours, context, g_outcomes[1]);
0414:     const Outcome& a = g_outcomes[0];
0415:     const Outcome& b = g_outcomes[1];
0416:     bool okA = a.childStatus >= 0 && WIFEXITED(a.childStatus) && WEXITSTATUS(a.childStatus) == 0;
0417:     bool okB = b.childStatus >= 0 && WIFEXITED(b.childStatus) && WEXITSTATUS(b.childStatus) == 0;
0418:     if (incomplete(a) || incomplete(b))
0419:     {
0420:         stats.incomplete++;
0421:         if (stats.incomplete <= 3)
0422:             host->log("    %s case %d: incomplete observation, original report %d issue %u, ours report %d issue %u\n",
0423:                       name, index, a.reportValid, a.capture.issue, b.reportValid, b.capture.issue);
0424:         return false;
0425:     }
0426:     if (!okA && !okB && a.childStatus == b.childStatus)
0427:     {
0428:         stats.bothFailed++;
0429:         return true;
0430:     }
0431:     if (okA && okB && a.capture.length == b.capture.length &&
0432:         std::memcmp(a.capture.data, b.capture.data, a.capture.length) == 0)
0433:     {
0434:         stats.same++;
0435:         return true;
0436:     }
0437:     stats.different++;
0438:     if (stats.different <= 3)
0439:     {
0440:         size_t at = 0;
0441:         while (at < a.capture.length && at < b.capture.length && a.capture.data[at] == b.capture.data[at])
0442:             at++;
0443:         host->log("    %s case %d: original status %d len %lu, ours status %d len %lu, first difference at %lu\n",
0444:                   name, index, a.status, (unsigned long)a.capture.length, b.status,
0445:                   (unsigned long)b.capture.length, (unsigned long)at);
0446:     }
0447:     return false;
0448: }
0449: 
0450: inline double seconds()
0451: {
0452:     struct timespec now;
0453:     clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &now);
0454:     return now.tv_sec + now.tv_nsec * 1e-9;
0455: }
